Steps.1: Check on schematic that 1.8V, 1V and 2.5V power rails supply the Ethernet transceiver.
Steps.2: Connect the hw_DAA to a DAA CS harness.
Steps.3: Connect the power supply to the DAA CS harness power input, using a DC power connector, banana cables, and crocodile clips (according to the attached diagram).
Steps.4: Switch on the power supply source.
Steps.5: Set 6.5V on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.6: Turn on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.8: Set up the multimeter as voltmeter. Ensure it is set to Auto-Range, Run/Hold and DC Voltage.
Steps.9: Connect the positive lead of the multimeter to one of the VDDIO_x (x=1,2,3) of the Ethernet transceiver and the negative lead to GND (at C309 pads).
Steps.10: Measure with the multimeter and check if it is supplied with 1.8V.
Steps.11: Connect the positive lead of the multimeter to one of the VDD1P0_x (x=1,2,3,4) of the Ethernet transceiver and the negative lead to GND (at C310 pads).
Steps.12: Measure with the multimeter and check if it is supplied with 1.0V.
Steps.13: Connect the positive lead of the multimeter to one of the VDDIO_x (x=1,2) of the Ethernet transceiver and the negative lead to GND (at C308 pads).
Steps.14: Measure with the multimeter and check if it is supplied with 2.5V.
Steps.15: Repeat the measurements with different voltages at the power supply source: 12V, 24V and 36V (using CH1 and CH2 of the power supply source connected in serial).
